name: Transcutaneous Neural Static Emitter
description:
The TNSE-5 projects a dense, skin-penetrating field of low-amplitude electromagnetic interference precisely tuned to the conduction velocity range of myelinated peripheral nerve fibers. Targets within the emission cone experience a sudden, total interruption of voluntary motor signals below the neck — the effect is not pain, not unconsciousness, but a clean, terrifying paralysis while the subject remains fully alert. The field does not affect the autonomic nervous system, so breathing and cardiac function continue normally.

The weapon's engineering achievement lies in its frequency-hopping emission architecture, which cycles through seventeen discrete interference bands per second to prevent nerve conduction from adapting or routing around the disruption. Earlier prototypes produced only transient effects as the nervous system compensated within seconds; the TNSE-5's cycling maintains paralysis consistently for the duration of continuous emission plus a residual window of two to four minutes after the field is removed. The emitter cone covers approximately a thirty-degree arc and can be swept across multiple targets.

Arcturus Defense Solutions designed the TNSE-5 for hostage extraction scenarios where a clean, non-lethal area-denial option was required in close proximity to protected personnel. The weapon never entered standard military procurement due to ethical review complications — specifically, the finding that sustained exposure beyond ninety seconds produced measurable long-term nerve conduction deficits in test subjects. Arcturus disputes this finding publicly and continues to sell to private clients under a confidential licensing structure.
legality: Prohibited (active military licensing exemption for contracted operators)
specifications:
effective range: 3–18 meters
emission cone: 30 degrees
power source: Modular high-frequency oscillator pack, 9 minutes continuous emission
paralysis onset: 0.3–0.8 seconds
residual effect duration: 2–4 minutes post-emission
weight: 4.4 kg
form factor: Shoulder-braced emitter with pivoting head and integral targeting display
long term risk: Nerve conduction deficit with exposures exceeding 90 seconds (contested by manufacturer)
tactical_use: Extraction teams use the TNSE-5 to freeze a room while principals are moved — one operator holds the emitter on target while others execute the extraction, then the emitter is withdrawn and the team is clear before the paralysis fades. Counter-kidnapping units favor it for rescues where target identification is uncertain and lethal force is not authorized. The weapon requires a stable firing position and is not suited to mobile engagements. Operators note that aware targets who know the effect is temporary can remain combative immediately upon recovery, requiring secondary restraint measures.
cultural_context: The TNSE-5 is a weapon of power in a very specific sense: it does not harm, it simply removes agency entirely, and the subject knows it. Among GLMZ's underground networks, rumors of 'the veil' circulate as a near-mythological threat — something that can take you without a mark, without a sound. Survivors of TNSE-5 deployments frequently report the experience as psychologically scarring in ways that conventional violence is not. The weapon has also found use in a small, disturbing black-market context that authorities have been reluctant to document formally.
known_users: A known fixer collective operating in Sector 2 who acquired a unit through a military surplus diversion
At least one documented criminal organization using it for abduction operations
story_hooks: A series of abductions in an upscale district share a common forensic signature — no struggle, no evidence, just missing people — and a medical examiner has quietly flagged the nerve profile.
An Arcturus contractor goes off-reservation with a TNSE-5 unit and the company needs it recovered before the licensing structure is exposed in a criminal investigation.
A survivor of a TNSE-5 deployment is offering significant payment to anyone who can acquire one for a purpose they won't specify.
Arcturus's internal research files on long-term nerve damage are for sale — someone inside the company wants the truth out, but the data is heavily encrypted and the seller is already being followed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, shoulder-mounted emitter resembling a hybrid between a directed-energy weapon and medical imaging equipment. The primary body is a reinforced cylinder with a flared emission head that rotates on a gimbal mount. Looks industrial, purpose-built, utterly devoid of ergonomic softness — all angles and functional geometry. The emitter crown features a radial array of emission nodes arranged like a abstract flower or tactical muzzle brake.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 62 cm (including shoulder stock), emitter head diameter 14 cm, width across pivoting gimbal assembly 18 cm. Barrel projection (emission cone focal length) approximately 8 cm from the head housing.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but manageable on shoulder rig — 4.4 kg feels substantial without being cumbersome, weight distributed toward the shoulder brace. Requires stable positioning; not a weapon for spray-and-pray ergonomics.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polymer composite frame with aluminum heat-sink collar around the emitter head. Steel gimbal mount and shoulder brace. Internal oscillator pack encased in ferrite-shielded aluminum housing.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed aluminum accents on the gimbal and heat vents. Worn in field examples show bare composite showing through high-contact areas. No glossy surfaces — all surfaces are functionally textured to reduce reflectivity.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, brushed aluminum accents, with dark charcoal polymer sections. Integral targeting display screen glows soft cyan when powered.
physical_description.grip_texture: Shoulder brace wrapped in rubberized tactical grip material with subtle knurling. The auxiliary grip forward of the emitter head is bare aluminum knurl, designed for left-hand stabilization during gimbal control.
distinctive_features: Radial emission node array on the crown (17 frequency-tuned emitter elements visible as slight raised nodes)
Gimbal-mounted pivoting head with full 360-degree horizontal sweep and 60-degree vertical articulation
Integral 4-inch tactical display screen showing emission frequency readout and cone targeting reticle
Heat-dissipation vents running the length of the barrel assembly (17 parallel ridges corresponding to frequency channels)
Safety interlock switch with three-position detent (SAFE / STANDBY / ACTIVE) molded into the trigger guard
Modular oscillator pack cartridge slot on the underside of the barrel with quick-release catch
Faint laser targeting dot (red wavelength) projected from the emitter crown center
Serial/batch number engraved on the shoulder brace in white fill
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS stamped on the shoulder brace in serif lettering. Smaller text: MODEL TNSE-5, MILITARY CONTRACT ONLY, and an ARCTURIAN star-glyph logo (stylized A in a circle) embossed on the left side of the housing. Confidential licensing label on the oscillator cartridge bay.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained examples show light scuffing on the composite, occasional carbon scoring around the emitter nodes from high-frequency discharge residue, and wear polishing on the gimbal pivot from constant repositioning. Operators typically keep the targeting display lens clean and the frequency-cycle indicator LED functional. Long-deployed units show stress marks on the shoulder-brace contact points.

The integral targeting display screen glows a pale cyan, showing frequency readout numerals. Shallow depth of field keeps the emission head in razor focus while the shoulder brace softens slightly in the background.
